sg-regs-2005-reg5.label: Special Guardianship Regulations 2005, reg 5
sg-regs-2005-reg5.holding: The council remains responsible for assessing support needs for three years from the making of the order.

sg-regs-2005-reg9.label: Special Guardianship Regulations 2005, reg 9
sg-regs-2005-reg9.holding: Financial support ceases in the circumstances set out in the regulation, including when the child reaches 18 unless the conditions for continuing are met.

dfe-guidance-2017-para65.label: DfE Special Guardianship Guidance (Jan 2017), para 65
dfe-guidance-2017-para65.note: Statutory guidance for local authorities on the Special Guardianship Regulations 2005 (as amended 2016), January 2017. Published 30 December 2005, last updated 26 January 2017. The Summer 2026 update has NOT landed as at 29 August 2026, so paragraph numbering is unchanged and this citation still lands correctly. The guidance's own front matter says it 'will next be reviewed in 2018' — it is eight years past its stated review date, and predates the full rollout of Universal Credit.

lewisham-2008.label: R (B) v Lewisham LBC [2008] EWHC 738 (Admin)
lewisham-2008.holding: Using the lower adoption allowance model was unlawful. Fostering allowances are the starting point.

kirklees-2010.label: Barrett v Kirklees MBC [2010] EWHC 467 (Admin)
kirklees-2010.holding: A flat two-thirds of the core fostering allowance was an unjustified departure from guidance.

merton-2012.label: R (TT) v Merton LBC [2012] EWHC 2055 (Admin)
merton-2012.holding: Blanket percentage deduction unlawful. BUT: no duty to pay every special guardian an allowance, and the means-test methodology itself was upheld as lawful.

tower-hamlets-2013.label: R (X) v Tower Hamlets LBC [2013] EWCA Civ 904
tower-hamlets-2013.holding: Paying family foster carers less than unrelated foster carers was unlawful. Former foster carers should not be worse off.

lgsco-devon-2024.label: LGSCO decision, Devon County Council (23 000 973, 25 January 2024)
lgsco-devon-2024.holding: The council was at fault for deducting Child Benefit from all special guardians on Universal Credit as a blanket rule, without looking at individual circumstances. It was ordered to recalculate and to refund deductions. Devon changed the policy with effect from 1 January 2024, and a later complaint about its current practice was not upheld.
lgsco-devon-2024.note: Paragraph 45 records 170 special guardians on means-tested benefits in the area, 92 not on benefits, and 125 where the council held no information. Read alongside lgsco-devon-24-003-172, which found the practice Devon operates NOW to be consistent with government guidance. Nothing on this site may imply Devon is currently at fault.

lgsco-southend-2020.label: LGSCO decision, Southend-on-Sea (19 003 363, 5 October 2020)
lgsco-southend-2020.holding: Reducing the whole allowance to 75% of the core fostering allowance in year one and 50% in year two misapplied the two-year transitional provision, which concerns the reward element only. Backdating of about 6,948 pounds was recommended, and the council estimated 37 other families were affected.

lgsco-north-tyneside-17002928.label: LGSCO public report, North Tyneside Council (17 002 928, 27 February 2018)
lgsco-north-tyneside-17002928.holding: Calculating a special guardianship allowance as a percentage of the fostering allowance was contrary to statutory guidance and case law. The council identified 171 families who may not have received the right support, and payments were backdated to November 2013.
lgsco-north-tyneside-17002928.note: Served from the web archive because the Ombudsman's own asset server times out on this PDF. Original address, kept as provenance: https://www.lgo.org.uk/assets/attach/4322/REPORT-17002928-N-Tyneside.pdf. A third copy sits in North Tyneside's own committee papers if both fail. The remedy was 200 pounds already paid plus a further 200 pounds each ordered, so 400 pounds each to two people. This is a February 2018 report, and it concerns the policy North Tyneside abolished that year. The archive URL previously carried no timestamp, so it was not a pinned capture. lgo.org.uk itself times out for this report, which is why the archive is used.

corambaaf-pn75.label: CoramBAAF Practice Note 75 - special guardianship financial support
corambaaf-pn75.holding: The DfE standardised means-test model is non-statutory and pre-dates Universal Credit.
corambaaf-pn75.note: Resolves publicly but sits on a members-area path, so it may be withdrawn without notice. A substitute for the one proposition we rely on it for, that the DfE means test model is not law, is tracked in watchlist.json as corambaaf-substitute: Lincolnshire's published assessment framework calls the model non-statutory guidance in its own words, which is a council conceding the point.

dfe-nma-2026-27.label: DfE National Minimum Allowance for foster carers, 2026 to 2027
dfe-nma-2026-27.note: Headed 'Weekly allowances for the tax year from 6 April 2026 to 5 April 2027'. Publishes three regional columns — London, South East, Rest of England — and no list of which authority sits in which.

dfe-nma-2025-26.label: DfE National Minimum Allowance for foster carers, 2025 to 2026
dfe-nma-2025-26.note: National Archives capture of 30 November 2025, headed "Weekly allowances for the tax year from 6 April 2025 to 5 April 2026". Matches the figures already held, exactly.

wg-nma-2026-27.label: The Fostering Network, national minimum allowances table, reproducing the Welsh 2026 to 2027 rates
wg-nma-2026-27.note: SECONDARY, and labelled as such. The Welsh Government letter has not been located after three searches. This table reproduces the figures; it does not originate them, which is why the Welsh section keeps verify: true. The separate citation wg-nma-2026-27-approval is the primary record that the allowance was approved, and it carries no rate table. Attributing the numbers to that page, as this entry previously did, put figures in the reader's hands under the authority of a document that does not state them.

sra-2026-27.label: Scottish Recommended Allowance for foster and kinship carers, Scottish Government, page updated 11 May 2026
sra-2026-27.holding: A national minimum for foster and kinship carers alike. Councils may pay more.
sra-2026-27.note: This page carries the 2026/27 figures and they match our table to the penny: 177.68, 206.71 for both middle bands, and 283.35. It is a live page that is updated in place each year, so it is the right source for the current year and the wrong one for any past year. For 2024/25 use sra-2024-25.

cb-ga-uprating-order-2026.label: Child Benefit and Guardian's Allowance Up-rating Order 2026

cb-ga-uprating-order-2025.label: Child Benefit and Guardian's Allowance Up-rating Order 2025

uc-two-child-limit-act-2026.label: Universal Credit (Removal of Two Child Limit) Act 2026 c.13

kinship-zones-2026.label: Kinship Zones - kinship allowance pilot (2026-2029)
kinship-zones-2026.holding: A pilot in seven English councils paying a non-means-tested allowance equal to the fostering National Minimum Allowance.
kinship-zones-2026.note: Community Care, 'Councils to test paying kinship carers an allowance', 27 February 2026. Seven authorities, up to three and a half years, evaluated by Foundations and Alma Economics. Labels the authorities by Government Office Region, including Wiltshire (South West).

dwp-benefit-rates-2026-27.label: DWP, Benefit and pension rates 2026 to 2027
dwp-benefit-rates-2026-27.note: First published 12 January 2026, updated 16 February 2026. Publishes 2025/26 and 2026/27 side by side. Source for the Income Support applicable amounts, the capital rules, the benefit cap and the Universal Credit child elements.

kinship-care-guidance-2024.label: DfE, Kinship Care: statutory guidance for local authorities (October 2024)
kinship-care-guidance-2024.holding: In calculating ongoing special guardianship financial support, the local authority should have regard to the fostering allowance that would have been paid if the child was fostered.
kinship-care-guidance-2024.note: Published 11 October 2024, replacing the 2010 Family and Friends Care guidance. A 2024 restatement of the para 65 principle, and so a fresher citation than the 2017 guidance for the single most important rule on this site.

lgsco-rochdale-2019.label: LGSCO decision, Rochdale MBC (17 010 167, May 2019), council's judicial review challenge dismissed
lgsco-rochdale-2019.holding: Grandparents were paid 119.18 pounds a week where the council's own fostering rate was 132 pounds, about 13 pounds a week short, under a policy departing from the statutory guidance without a rational explanation. Backdating to November 2013 was recommended.
lgsco-rochdale-2019.note: The council challenged the finding in the High Court in December 2019. Permission was refused, the challenge was dismissed and costs were awarded against it, which is what makes this decision safe to rely on. Ombudsman news item confirming that outcome: https://www.lgo.org.uk/information-centre/news/2019/dec/rochdale-council-s-legal-challenge-rejected-and-it-must-now-consider-ombudsman-s-recommendations. Reference corrected from an earlier entry that carried no decision number and linked to a Shropshire policy PDF. Wording corrected on 3 September 2026. The Ombudsman's decision survived; the council's challenge to it was refused permission and dismissed with costs. "Upheld on judicial review" read as though a court had affirmed something on review, which is not what happened.

sg-regs-2005-reg13.label: Special Guardianship Regulations 2005, reg 13(2)
sg-regs-2005-reg13.holding: Reg 13(2): in determining the amount of financial support the local authority MUST take account of any other grant, benefit, allowance or resource available to the person. It does not name Child Benefit. It imposes a duty to take other benefits into account, of which Child Benefit is one.
sg-regs-2005-reg13.note: Refined by the legal review of 2 September 2026. Cite reg 13(2) for the DUTY TO TAKE ACCOUNT of other benefits, and Barrett v Kirklees for the DEDUCTION itself: the court said councils should pay in line with the fostering allowance "(with the deduction of Child Benefit if appropriate)", recorded at paragraph 10 of the North Tyneside report. Do not attribute the Child Benefit deduction to the text of reg 13, because it is not there and a council lawyer will say so. The site's position is unchanged: what Devon got wrong was applying it to everyone without individual consideration.

north-tyneside-decision-2025.label: North Tyneside Council, Decision Record: Foster Care, Special Guardianship, Adoption and Child Arrangement Order Allowance Increases
north-tyneside-decision-2025.holding: Special guardianship allowances are uplifted alongside fostering allowances, with London and South East weighting applied in line with the recommended minimum levels. All uplifts take effect from 1 April 2025.
north-tyneside-decision-2025.note: Julie Firth, Director of Children's Services, 21 March 2025. Confirms the post-2018 equivalence-to-fostering position, and that this council applies uplifts from 1 April rather than the DfE's 6 April tax year.

shropshire-sg-policy-2021.label: Shropshire Council, Special Guardianship Allowances Policy (Cabinet, 8 February 2021)
shropshire-sg-policy-2021.note: Includes backdated payments to special guardians of previously looked-after children, and cites the Rochdale LGSCO report as the reason for the policy review.

lincolnshire-sg-framework.label: Lincolnshire County Council, Special Guardianship Allowance Assessment Framework
lincolnshire-sg-framework.holding: Distinguishes the statutory 'Special Guardianship Guidance' from the non-statutory 'Standardised means test model for adoption and special guardianship financial support'.
lincolnshire-sg-framework.note: A council, in its own published policy, classifying the DfE means-test model as non-statutory. The best available citation for MEANS_TEST_MODEL_OUTDATED. Also publishes a full worked example of the calculation.

derby-sg-scheme.label: Derby City Council, Special Guardianship Orders and Derby Support Scheme
derby-sg-scheme.holding: A Special Guardianship Order allowance is set at the equivalent of Derby's basic fostering rate for a child of that age.

fostering-news-2025-uplifts.label: Fostering news, '2025 Allowance Uplifts Across the UK'
fostering-news-2025-uplifts.holding: Records the 2025/26 Welsh National Minimum Allowance as £224 (0-4), £204 (5-10 and 11-15), £255 (16-17).
fostering-news-2025-uplifts.note: Secondary source, 15 September 2025. Used only to corroborate that the Welsh band inversion is genuinely published, not to set a rate.

fostering-network-allowances.label: The Fostering Network, Foster Care Allowances
fostering-network-allowances.holding: In February 2026 the Welsh Government announced an uplift of 2.2% to allowances for 2026/27.
fostering-network-allowances.note: Secondary source, used to corroborate the Welsh uplift percentage.

parliament-wq-14259.label: UK Parliament written question 14259 (National Minimum Allowance uplifts)
parliament-wq-14259.holding: The National Minimum Allowance was uplifted by 6.88% for 2024/25, following 12.43% in 2023/24.
parliament-wq-14259.note: DfE answer of 13 November 2024. Records the uplift percentage only — the 2024/25 table itself is still unsourced, and must NOT be reconstructed from this figure.

dfe-nma-2024-25.label: DfE National Minimum Allowance for foster carers, 2024 to 2025 (National Archives snapshot)
dfe-nma-2024-25.holding: Weekly allowances for the tax year from 6 April 2024 to 5 April 2025, by region and age band. This guidance applies to England.
dfe-nma-2024-25.note: The live GOV.UK page now shows the current year, so this is the UK Government Web Archive copy captured on 6 September 2024, when the 2024/25 table was current. Open the URL and choose a snapshot from within the 2024/25 year to see it. Figures transcribed as printed, not derived from the 6.88% uplift. Previously pointed at a National Archives wildcard search, which resolves to a list of captures rather than to the page that was read. Now the fixed capture of 2 March 2025.

lgsco-devon-24-003-172.label: LGSCO decision, Devon County Council (24 003 172), not upheld
lgsco-devon-24-003-172.holding: A later complaint about Devon's deductions was not upheld. The Ombudsman found the practice consistent with government guidance, the council paying its maximum allowance less child-related benefits.
lgsco-devon-24-003-172.note: Held on file specifically so the site cannot imply Devon is currently at fault. Any wording about Devon must carry both this and the January 2024 report.

lgsco-22-018-116.label: LGSCO decision, friends and family carers (22 018 116)
lgsco-22-018-116.holding: Fault for not following the guidance on how much to pay, and for not considering exceptional circumstances.

lgsco-22-011-906.label: LGSCO decision, friends and family carers (22 011 906)
lgsco-22-011-906.holding: Concerns a 2020 policy change and how it affected the calculation of allowances.

lgsco-20-005-985.label: LGSCO decision, fostering (20 005 985)
lgsco-20-005-985.holding: Squarely about the two-year transitional provision and the skills or reward element ending two years after the special guardianship order.

sra-2024-25.label: Scottish Recommended Allowance, rates announced 29 August 2023, unchanged for 2024/25
sra-2024-25.holding: A national minimum for foster and kinship carers alike. Councils may pay more.
sra-2024-25.note: These rates were introduced in August 2023 and were not uprated for 2024/25, so they are the 2024/25 figures. Take them from this release or an archived capture, never from the live gov.scot page, which now shows 2026/27. gov.scot gives 11-15 as the same as 5-10; some local authority reproductions show a higher 11-15 figure. The primary source wins.

sra-implementation-review.label: Scottish Government, Foster and kinship carers, Scottish Recommended Allowance: implementation review
sra-implementation-review.holding: Records that there was no uplift to payments in the financial year 2024/25.
sra-implementation-review.note: No permanent address located for the review document itself. It is the evidence that the August 2023 rates stood through 2024/25, so it is recorded rather than dropped. The same review says there was no indication of an uplift in 2025/26, which is an expectation and not a published rate, so 2025/26 stays unsourced.

devon-sgo-procedures-2024.label: Devon County Council, Applications for Special Guardianship Orders (procedures manual), last updated 24 October 2024
devon-sgo-procedures-2024.holding: Devon uses the standardised means-test model with the living costs disregard set at 100% of the Income Support applicable amount, states that paying a fixed percentage of the fostering allowance would not be lawful, and stopped deducting Child Benefit from special guardians on means-tested benefits from 1 January 2024.

leeds-sgo-support-offer-2024.label: Leeds City Council, Revised Special Guardianship Support Offer, cover report, 1 March 2024
leeds-sgo-support-offer-2024.holding: Under the revised offer, carers of children subject to non-agency orders who already receive a means-tested benefit are to receive support that is not means tested.
leeds-sgo-support-offer-2024.note: Leeds's own operational manual states that its special guardianship financial support information is under review, so this offer is not a settled position. Decision record: https://democracy.leeds.gov.uk/ieDecisionDetails.aspx?AIId=95875

ciw-nma-bulletin-2023-24.label: Care Inspectorate Wales, National Minimum Allowances for Foster Carers 2023 to 2024, bulletin of 27 January 2023
ciw-nma-bulletin-2023-24.holding: Welsh national minimum allowances are issued as bilingual bulletins produced by Care Inspectorate Wales on behalf of the Welsh Government, addressed to local authorities and independent fostering providers, setting rates the Welsh Government expects to be applied from 1 April.
ciw-nma-bulletin-2023-24.note: This is the confirmed example of the publication route, which is what was missing. The rate table inside the bulletin is an image, so any year retrieved this way has to be read by a person. The bulletins for 2024/25 and 2026/27 have not been located.

wg-codes-consultation-2026.label: Welsh Government, consultation on changes to two codes of practice: Part 6 and Special Guardianship Orders, 12 February to 7 April 2026
wg-codes-consultation-2026.holding: Draft revisions would require all services to pay the national minimum allowance and introduce an enhanced fostering allowance and fee.
wg-codes-consultation-2026.note: DRAFT, consultation closed 7 April 2026, outcome not published. Nothing on this site may state these as the law. The Special Guardianship Orders code is being revised alongside the Part 6 code and is directly relevant to the Wales pages when the outcome lands.

ni-model-scheme-2024-25.label: Department of Health (Northern Ireland), Foster care allowances, Model Scheme 2024-25
ni-model-scheme-2024-25.holding: Sets the weekly foster care scale rates in Northern Ireland from 1 April 2024 at 149, 166, 187 and 219 pounds across four age bands.
ni-model-scheme-2024-25.note: Section 1, SCALE RATES. The same document prints a REDUCED RATES table on page 2 (108, 120, 135, 158) which is the scale rate less pocket money and clothing, used only for enhanced allowances and short break payments. Do not confuse the two.

wg-nma-2024-25.label: Welsh Government, National Minimum Allowances for foster carers 2024 to 2025, circular of 26 February 2024
wg-nma-2024-25.holding: Sets the Welsh national minimum allowances from 1 April 2024 at 218 pounds for ages 0 to 4, 199 pounds for 5 to 15 and 248 pounds for 16 and over, a rise of 3 per cent.
wg-nma-2024-25.note: A copy of the Welsh Government letter of 26 February 2024, on Welsh Government letterhead and signed by Alistair Davey, hosted by The Fostering Network. Located by the review of 2 September 2026. It is the primary document, not a report of it, which is what makes it usable. A gov.wales or Care Inspectorate Wales copy would be better and is still wanted: these go out as email bulletins, so one may not exist publicly. Tracked in watchlist.json as ciw-nma-bulletins.

sg-regs-2005-reg6-2-b.label: Special Guardianship Regulations 2005, reg 6(2)(b)
sg-regs-2005-reg6-2-b.holding: The specific provision on taking a child's needs into account when deciding financial support, including any disability or the consequences of earlier abuse or neglect.
sg-regs-2005-reg6-2-b.note: Cited specifically rather than as reg 6 as a whole, on the reviewer's instruction of 1 September 2026, so an enhancement request points at the sub paragraph it rests on.

ca1989-s14f-3.label: Children Act 1989, s.14F(3)
ca1989-s14f-3.holding: A local authority MAY assess a person's needs for special guardianship support services on request, but MUST do so where that person is of a description prescribed in regulations. The duty to assess therefore does not exist in the Act alone: it needs reg 11(1) to supply the prescribed description.
ca1989-s14f-3.note: Identified by the legal review of 2 September 2026, answering the question parked on 1 September. The site previously rested the duty on reg 6, which governs when financial support is payable rather than when an assessment is owed. Cite this together with sg-regs-2005-reg11; neither carries the claim alone.

sg-regs-2005-reg11.label: Special Guardianship Regulations 2005, reg 11
sg-regs-2005-reg11.holding: Prescribes, for the purposes of s.14F(3), the persons at whose request an assessment MUST be carried out: reg 11(1)(a) a relevant child looked after, or looked after immediately before the order; (b) a special guardian or prospective special guardian of such a child; (c) a parent of such a child. Where reg 11(1) does not apply, reg 11(2) to (3) require the authority, if minded not to assess, to give notice with reasons and allow representations.

sg-regs-2005-reg18.label: Special Guardianship Regulations 2005, reg 18(2)(a)
sg-regs-2005-reg18.holding: The local authority must review financial support payable periodically on receipt of the annual statement mentioned in reg 10. The trigger is receipt of the statement, not the passage of twelve months.
sg-regs-2005-reg18.note: Replaces sg-regs-2005-reg10-11, which was wrong for this purpose: reg 10 imposes a duty on the CARER to supply an annual statement, and reg 11 is the request for assessment. Reg 17(2) carries the words "in any event, at least annually" but reg 17(1) applies it to support other than periodic financial support, so it does not cover the allowance. Corrected by the legal review of 2 September 2026.

sg-regs-2005-reg10.label: Special Guardianship Regulations 2005, reg 10
sg-regs-2005-reg10.holding: Conditions. Reg 10(1)(b) requires the special guardian to agree to supply an annual statement of their circumstances. That statement is what triggers the review duty in reg 18(2)(a).

ni-model-scheme-2025-26.label: Department of Health (Northern Ireland), Model Scheme 2025-26, Section 1, Foster Care Allowances
ni-model-scheme-2025-26.holding: SCALE RATES from 1 April 2025: 155.00, 173.00, 194.00 and 228.00 a week.
ni-model-scheme-2025-26.note: The same PDF prints a REDUCED RATES table for enhanced allowances and short breaks. That is not the allowance. The scale rate is the one pinned by test.

sra-2025-26.label: Scottish Government, Scottish Recommended Allowance: information for carers and professionals, page updated 27 June 2025
sra-2025-26.holding: 2025-26 weekly allowances, backdated to 1 April 2025: 0 to 4 at 171.17, 5 to 10 at 199.14, 11 to 15 at 199.14, 16 and over at 272.97. The same page states that no family should be worse off, that the allowance is the higher of what is currently paid or the SRA, and that the SRA does not apply to continuing care.
sra-2025-26.note: Archived capture of 15 October 2025. The live page now shows 2026/27, so this is the only route to the 2025/26 figures. It also settles a conflict: a council reproduction showing 207.60 at 11-15 was reprinting 2023/24 rates.

dfe-nma-2024-25-second-capture.label: GOV.UK, Help with the cost of fostering, capture of 2 March 2025
dfe-nma-2024-25-second-capture.holding: Weekly allowances for the tax year from 6 April 2024 to 5 April 2025: London 191/195/217/248/289, South East 183/189/208/238/278, Rest of England 165/170/187/213/249.
dfe-nma-2024-25-second-capture.note: A SECOND capture, at a different date, of the table already recovered from the 6 September 2024 snapshot. Two independent captures, same figures. Kept because a transcription confirmed twice from separate captures is the strongest evidence this project has for a historic rate table.

dfe-no-minimum-after-18.label: GOV.UK, Help with the cost of fostering, on allowances after a child is old enough to leave foster care
dfe-no-minimum-after-18.holding: States in terms: "There is no minimum allowance when your child is old enough to leave foster care."
dfe-no-minimum-after-18.note: Located by the research of 2 September 2026 while capturing the 2025/26 table. The turning-18 page had no source at all for the post-18 position.

wg-nma-2026-27-approval.label: Welsh Government, decision reports 2026, recording ministerial approval of the National Minimum Allowances for 2026 to 2027
wg-nma-2026-27-approval.holding: Records in Welsh that the Minister for Children and Social Care approved the National Minimum Allowances for Foster Carers for 2026 to 2027. Establishes that the allowance exists and was approved. Contains NO rate table.
